en: You know my name?
Of course! You've been a good customer. How's that piece of armor holding up?
Huh? Wait. I don't see it on you... Shit, did someone take it?
Well ain't that a bummer. You're slower than you used to be, huh? Be careful out there.
Why are you here?
Huh? Because this is my post? People from all corners of Zalesye know I'm right here with some great deals.
Since I specialize in armor, it's important that everyone with a mind for survival knows where to find me at all times. First thing to get nicked during a gunfight, after all.
You know that too well, don't ya...
So I *did* get my armor stolen...
... That sucks. Sold it to you just the other day...
Listen... Dear Ves – my wife Vesna, that is – has been helping me out a lot lately. We've got a pretty good scheme going, and she's helping me expand my inventory, so...
Shouldn't hurt to give you a bit of a discount. Just keep it on the hush-hush and all. Ok?
Vesna is your wife?
Yes! Have you met her? She's the best. We help each other out a lot.
Has its ups and downs, being together with someone all the time. I'm sure it would weird the hell out of a Vulture.
But ultimately... Can't imagine life in Zalesye without her. It's a strange feeling...
How did you and Vesna get together?
Well, I did some business with her, essentially. She needed fabrics that were a part of some armor I was reselling.
I made her a good deal and asked her what it was all for. She mentioned she was a member of the Rada and was helping them out with some charity...
Seeing her eyes light up like that, at that moment... Talking about helping out her peers... I was hooked.
Why haven't you joined the Rada?
Don't wanna join any one specific group. You do that as a merchant and next thing you know your entire business model is partial to specific people. Not a good mode of operations.
I want everybody's business; everyone's a friend! Doesn't matter if I like 'em, if I refuse someone service I am no longer a real merchant.
And then it'll just take a million years more for me to get rich and hop on a Great Train or whatever – escape this hellhole...
You mentioned the "Great Trains"?
Well, it's a bit embarrassing, but... I really do believe they exist. I mean, this world is full of strangeness... Take the Mist, for example.
I feel like the Mist has power. The Mist... Can do anything. It twists us in a magical and cruel way, as it wills.
There has to be a force just like that, but... For good. Y'know? Some magic to counter the Mist – like the Great Trains, flying towards the East...
Want to know more about Great Trains.
Interesting, isn't it? This whole story.
I've got to get going.
What are the Great Trains, exactly?
As a Vulture, I'm sure you've heard it: the clanky whistle of a ghost ride, emanating from the disjointed tracks that go from the deep Dola to Zakrajev Line just above us.

An impossible metallic rattle of a wagon moving between other wagons, through containers and bits of rail-less land; the silhouette of some great magical device, or perhaps a product of pre-War science – mankind's last great achievement, still levitating a chosen few in its rusty carcass...
They serve to take us East, Rodion. They appear to us the same way the Acolytes talk of Jesus reappearing from the dead... A resurrection that means salvation for us all – or so I understand.
They take us East... To Wyraj?
Indeed. A land with no Mist. Nothing in the world like it – at least not here, in Rhos.
That's impossible.

So is a Mist that corrupts man and animal alike into unsightly beasts. So is the defeat of our kind by our own hand – so are a lot of things that happened not *today*, not *yesterday*, but *throughout history*. History itself has the power to do the impossible, and we're *always* living through it.
How do you get aboard a Great Train?
From what I've heard, and felt... It's wealth. Being able to afford it. Becoming the richest motherfucker in Zalesye... Then leaving it behind.

Maybe it's a dog-eat-dog world after all, and the rich shall triumph over the poor. Or maybe it's about letting go... Get to the top only to give it up and go to a mystical place where that doesn't even matter. Reminds me of the Church's teachings.
Maybe it's just material necessity for a Great Train which is non-magical, simply a bit of machinery. I don't really know.
Either way... Gotta bust your ass to get there, I suppose. Nothing's easy in this world.
Have you ever seen one?
I think I have, yes. Sometimes I tell myself I'm sure, but fuck, I don't think that's fair.
I've seen its silhouette, when I went the furthest into the Dola I ever have. Heard its sounds, its whistling... The rattle of some invisible railroad.

I've seen it in my dreams and in what I think was my waking life. Had the wagon's shadows in the corner of my eye. I've even felt its inside walls supporting my back, shaking gently, a warm blanket over my knees...
Before you think I'm crazy, friend – I know for sure the sounds were real. That, at least. Too constant for me to doubt them. And I'm sure you've heard them too.
About something else.
I've gotta go now.
Rodion. Looking not too shabby. Remember me, Yefim? Got new merch, y'should see it.
Hey, Rodion. Looking to buy?
How's it going?
Hey there!
Wanna talk.
Let's talk a bit.
Got something to talk about.
Want to see your wares.
How about we trade?
Have some stuff to trade.
Let's get into it.
Time to trade, then.
Got plenty in stock for you.
Let's do this.
Great! Let's.
See you later.
Take care, Rodion.
Take care out there.
Be careful. See ya.
Talk to you later.
Sounds easy enough.
Well, not so sure about that. But I'm glad you accepted.
I need to think on it.
Sure, but please don't leave me hanging, here.
Do you have anything else?
Glad to help.
Let me know if something else comes up.
I'll find what you need.
I'm sure you will – just be careful out there.
Need to think about it.
Ok, I'm not in a rush.
Hmm. Anything else you need?
A present, huh...
Take care.
It's been hard getting hold of everything me and Vesna need. There's supplies I need in order to keep givin' you these sweet deals, hehe. Wanna help out?
Hardest thing about this job – the inconsistency. Suddenly my inventory's full of holes. What do you say to finding me some supplies?
You got all of it! Wouldn't expect less of ya. Here's your pay.
Nice, this is going to be a huge help for the week. Thank you!
You did it – nice going, Rodion. Here you go.

I don't always have my head on straight when negotiating... Passed on a couple items last week, been regretting it – could you find them for me?
You found just what I needed. This'll make a great present!
Nice... This'll make her happy...
Oh, great! Yeah, this'll do just fine. Should I just give it to her like this?... Wrap it, maybe...
I don't have any requests right now, Rodion. Maybe tomorrow.

Well, I trust you, so here goes: Palatines found an old military barracks in a bunker down Southeast, full of armor and clothing... And me and my dear Ves desperately need the extra inventory.
Ok, but the reward had better be worth it.

They've just sent a detachment nearby to keep the bunker "safe." Probably not the friendliest bunch, but I can't think of how to get there without their key. Hell, don't even exactly know where they are.
That's a shame, friend. You'll have to contend with my dwindling inventory, right after the Palatines failed to protect you and your valuable gear...
I know it's a lot to ask, but I want that bunker found, breached and cleared. Can't do any of that on my own, gotta work all day. So... Will you help?
Sounds too involved.
I don't doubt that for a second; hopefully you'll find the whole thing was worth it when you're straddling around with a nice piece of armor a few weeks from now.
Palatines won't be happy about this.
Oh, err, of course. You were more directly involved and all. But Vultures have their own ways of getting back on someone's good side, no?
Soon they'll be buying back some of that equipment from me without even realizing it!
Anyway, here's what I owe ya. Do take care of yourself and come back later for some extra goodies in the shop.
Alone? No, never alone. I have some contacts who can help with those runs. There's more investments to make before this venture pays off.

Heard you've been making moves out there, so I knew it was just a matter of time! Most other Vultures aren't resourceful enough to pull this off, y'know. Do look forward to some discounts in the future!
That can only happen if I get paid.
This was exhausting.
Oh, right. Here you go, Rodion. And come back some other time to check out the new inventory, alright?
Worried about myself, mostly.
Oh, I'll be fine; got close friends in their ranks. 'Sides, right now they're too concerned about the Gunners to care about some bunker so far away...
Will you be alright sneaking into that bunker alone?
Asking nicely for the key won't cut it, unless someone high up in their hierarchy owes you a favor or something.
Haven't seen the door myself, so I don't know if it can be "breached," per se. Bet a Mechanist would know, though.
Any ideas on how to breach the bunker?
I'll get to it, then.
I'll be waiting for your report then. Do take care and uh, keep all this between us, would you.
My source says you'll find that bunker going down and East from here. The soldier camp should be around there, somewhere safe, good vantage point...
Going against Palatines? Thought everyone was a friend.
What are the steps here, exactly?
I need the locations of both the bunker and the camp – gotta know where it is so I can avoid it when it's time to get the goods. It has to be clear of Mutants, too.
Other than that, you know the drill, Rodion. I'm well aware of how Vultures operate: they either go unnoticed or cause a huge ruckus in their wake. No middle ground.
Hey, having friends in the Palatines is how I got this tip in the first place. But I still gotta get my hands dirty sometimes, that's just a part of the job.
Oh, it definitely is. Again, I realize I'm asking a lot. Wouldn't be offering the gig if I didn't think we both stand to gain from it, though.
Better be a lifetime discount after all that work...
Oh, it will be. Both myself and Ves will make sure to share some of the goods with you, plus some pay.
I'll take that as a yes! As for a lifetime discount, no promises. But there'll be something, for sure.
